titleEn: Agrifood corporates find a new model for financing regenerative agriculture via Soil Capital partnership
titleZh: 农食企业通过Soil Capital合作找到再生农业融资新模式
summaryZh: Royal Canin与Roquette通过Soil Capital合作，共同投资其小麦来源农场，分担农民向再生农业转型的财务负担。Soil Capital作为第三方MRV桥梁，协调两家公司不同的碳核算方法，避免双重计算。该模式覆盖法国60多个农场、4700多公顷，农民获得70%的土壤碳信用收益，为供应链协同融资再生农业提供了可复制模板。
featuredReason: 该案例展示了供应链协同融资再生农业的创新模式，通过第三方MRV解决碳核算方法差异问题，对智慧畜牧中涉及饲料原料可持续采购和碳足迹管理的企业具有参考价值。
contentFull:
Agrifood has long debated who should pay for farmers to switch to regenerative agriculture practices. Royal Canin and Roquette now offer a new approach that takes the financial weight away from farmers and spreads it along the supply chain.

Ingredients supplier Roquette provides Mars-owned Royal Canin with wheat for its pet food products. Via a partnership with Soil Capital, the two companies will now co-invest in the farms from which they source that wheat.

The transition to on-farm regenerative practices typically needs upfront capital to finance things like new equipment, cover crops, and adapting to new crop rotations. Currently, farmers either bear this cost themselves or are part of a corporate insetting program that may or may not offer economical support.

“We believe that a joint investment model is the most effective way to drive large-scale adoption of regenerative agriculture,” Magali Amouroux, sustainability manager at Roquette, tells AgFunderNews.

“By sharing both the costs and the value created across the supply chain, this approach helps reduce the financial burden on farmers, aligns incentives among stakeholders and ensures a fair distribution of benefits.”

Bridge over different methodologies 

Soil Capital helps companies monitor, measure and report on regenerative agriculture outcomes in addition to providing agronomic expertise to farmers.

For this partnership, it plays the crucial role of a bridge joining two distinct methodologies with one independently verified farm-level dataset.

Different companies use different methodologies to calculate the carbon footprint of a product or ingredient. These are typically based on the company’s sector. Royal Canin uses economic allocation, most common to the pet food industry, while Roquette uses mass balance allocation, the standard for the starch industry.

The difference in methodologies means these companies’ figures are not directly comparable and could lead to discrepancies and double counting outcomes.

“What you need is a third party that has a robust MRV [monitoring, reporting, and verification] framework that is compliant to external guidelines,” explains Luc Beerens, global director for sustainable sourcing at Royal Canin.

In this case, Soil Capital will handle the monitoring, measuring, and data collection on the farm as well as verification of that data. All farm data undergo third-party verification under ISO 14064-2 by TÜV Rheinland, ensuring methodological integrity through independent annual audits.

The idea is to allow the two companies to continue operating with their own methodologies while working off the same neutral dataset.

“As long as you base it on the right farmer data, there’s no you know double counting,” Beerens tells AgFunderNews.

“By managing data traceability for both companies, Soil Capital enabled us to work together on the same program while maintaining our respective accounting methodologies and avoiding double counting of environmental benefits,” adds Amouroux.

Replicating the model

The partnership will cover more than 60 farms covering over 4,700 hectares in France’s wheat supply shed.

Results from the transition (e.g., carbon sequestered) will generate Soil Capital Credits, of which farmers will receive 70%, according to the companies.

Beyond financial support for farmers, the partnership will help the companies become compliant with the fast-changing regulatory landscape in Europe, says Beerens.

For example, the Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming (CRCF) certification Europe’s first government-backed framework for carbon removals. The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CRCD) requires companies to report on environmental impact across their value chains.

“We are building partnerships that are needed when [these regulations] come into play,” he notes. “We obviously need need more.”

To that end, both companies are currently exploring ways to replicate this co-financing model with other companies.

“We are in this for the long-term transition to reduce our carbon footprint, but also to make our supply sheds more resilient,” notes Beerens.

“We would like to engage more customers who share our sustainability ambitions to jointly finance the agricultural transition while ensuring its benefits and risks are shared along the value chain,” adds Amouroux.

“This partnership with Royal Canin demonstrates that differences in carbon allocation methodologies do not have to be a barrier for collaboration. It provides a replicable model that could be extended to other crops and geographies.”

translationZh:
农食行业长期以来一直在争论谁应该为农民转向再生农业实践买单。Royal Canin和Roquette现在提供了一种新方法，将财务负担从农民身上移开，并沿着供应链分摊。

原料供应商Roquette向Mars旗下的Royal Canin提供用于宠物食品的小麦。通过与Soil Capital的合作，这两家公司现在将共同投资于他们采购小麦的农场。

向农场再生实践的转型通常需要前期资本来资助新设备、覆盖作物和适应新的作物轮作等事项。目前，农民要么自己承担这笔费用，要么参与企业内嵌项目，而该项目可能提供也可能不提供经济支持。

“我们相信联合投资模式是推动再生农业大规模采用的最有效方式，”Roquette可持续发展经理Magali Amouroux告诉AgFunderNews。

“通过在整个供应链中分担成本和创造的价值，这种方法有助于减轻农民的财务负担，协调利益相关者的激励措施，并确保利益的公平分配。”

**跨越不同方法论的桥梁**

Soil Capital帮助企业监测、测量和报告再生农业成果，此外还向农民提供农艺专业知识。

对于这一合作，它扮演着关键角色，即用一套独立验证的农场级数据集将两种不同的方法论连接起来。

不同公司使用不同的方法来计算产品或原料的碳足迹。这些通常基于公司所属行业。Royal Canin使用经济分配法，这是宠物食品行业最常见的做法，而Roquette使用质量平衡分配法，这是淀粉行业的标准。

方法论的差异意味着这些公司的数据不能直接比较，可能导致差异和结果的双重计算。

“你需要的是一个拥有稳健MRV（监测、报告和验证）框架且符合外部准则的第三方，”Royal Canin全球可持续采购总监Luc Beerens解释道。

在本案例中，Soil Capital将负责农场层面的监测、测量和数据收集以及数据验证。所有农场数据均通过TÜV Rheinland根据ISO 14064-2进行第三方验证，通过独立的年度审计确保方法论的完整性。

其理念是让两家公司继续按照各自的方法论运作，同时基于同一套中立数据集工作。

“只要基于正确的农民数据，就不会有双重计算，”Beerens告诉AgFunderNews。

“通过为两家公司管理数据可追溯性，Soil Capital使我们能够在同一项目上合作，同时保持各自的核算方法，避免环境效益的双重计算，”Amouroux补充道。

**复制该模式**

该合作将覆盖法国小麦供应区超过60个农场、4700多公顷土地。

据两家公司称，转型成果（例如碳封存）将产生Soil Capital Credits，农民将获得其中的70%。

Beerens表示，除了对农民的财务支持外，该合作还将帮助公司遵守欧洲快速变化的监管环境。

例如，碳移除和碳农业（CRCF）认证是欧洲首个政府支持的碳移除框架。企业可持续发展报告指令（CSRD）要求公司报告其价值链的环境影响。

“我们正在建立这些法规出台时所需的合作伙伴关系，”他指出。“我们显然需要更多。”

为此，两家公司目前正在探索与其他公司复制这种共同融资模式的方式。

“我们致力于长期转型以减少碳足迹，同时也使我们的供应区更具韧性，”Beerens指出。

“我们希望吸引更多认同我们可持续发展目标的客户，共同资助农业转型，同时确保其收益和风险沿价值链共享，”Amouroux补充道。

“与Royal Canin的合作表明，碳分配方法论的差异不必成为合作的障碍。它提供了一个可复制的模式，可以扩展到其他作物和地区。”
author: Jennifer Marston
